findings.issue_text: [BUG] enableSqlExpressions() unconditionally returns false (the second `return false` is reached for every caller regardless of the flag state), so every QueryTypeSQL query returns the error "sqlExpressions is not implemented" even when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled. Users who enable the sqlExpressions feature flag still get a hard error on every SQL expression query; the feature gate is dead code and the feature can never be exercised.

[BUG] The flag check logic is inverted with respect to its variable name: `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` sets enabled to true when the flag is DISABLED, so even if the final unconditional return were fixed to `return enabled`, the gate would reject queries when the flag is on and allow them when it is off. Any fix that keeps this expression (e.g. changing only the last return to `return enabled`) ships the feature backwards: enabled-flag users are blocked and disabled-flag users reach an always-erroring stub DB.

[BUG] SQLCommand.Execute now calls the stub NewInMemoryDB() whose QueryFramesInto always returns errors.New("not implemented"), so every SQL command execution fails even though this call site is not gated on the FlagSqlExpressions check that guards the reader path. Any caller that constructs a SQLCommand directly (bypassing the reader's QueryTypeSQL gate) gets a guaranteed runtime failure instead of a query result; previously this path executed real DuckDB queries via go-duck.

[BUG] TablesList now runs its json_serialize_sql command against the stub DB whose RunCommands always returns errors.New("not implemented"), breaking this function entirely while the diff removes the only dependency (go-duck) that could satisfy it. TablesList returns an error for every input; any existing unit test in pkg/expr/sql that asserts parsed table names now fails at CI, and any production caller of TablesList is broken.

[BUG] enableSqlExpressions unconditionally returns false — the function body computes the flag check then discards it with a hardcoded `return false`, so the SQL-expressions feature can never be enabled. Every SQL-type expression query fails with "sqlExpressions is not implemented" even when the FlagSqlExpressions feature toggle is explicitly enabled; the feature gate is dead code and the gate-based rollout cannot ever be turned on without another code change.

[BUG] The flag check is inverted: `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` assigns true when the flag is DISABLED, naming a variable `enabled` for the disabled state. Even if the final `return false` were corrected to return the computed value, the logic would enable SQL expressions only for instances that have NOT enabled the flag — the exact opposite of the intended gating — silently enabling an unimplemented feature on default instances.

[BUG] SQLCommand.Execute now calls the stub DB whose QueryFramesInto always returns errors.New("not implemented"), so every previously-working SQL expression query breaks at runtime. Any existing user with saved SQL expressions (previously executed via go-duck) gets a failed query on every dashboard refresh/alert evaluation after this change; alert rules using SQL expressions silently stop evaluating successfully — a functional regression with no migration path in the diff.

[BUG] TablesList now delegates to the stub NewInMemoryDB whose RunCommands always returns "not implemented", so the SQL parser path is permanently broken. Any caller of sql.TablesList gets an error for every input; the SQL-parsing capability (table extraction for validation) is silently removed while its exported function and call sites remain, leaving dead code that always fails.

[ADVISORY] The new sql.DB is a ships-inert placeholder: all three methods are hardcoded stubs, yet the diff wires it into two live call paths (Execute and TablesList) instead of leaving the old go-duck implementation in place. The diff removes a working dependency (scottlepp/go-duck) and replaces it with non-functional stubs; operators and users get hard failures where queries previously succeeded, and the 'Advanced SQL Analytics Framework' delivers zero functioning behavior — the acceptance criterion 'SQL expressions execute' is unmet.

[ADVISORY] The new gate-and-error path in ReadQuery has no test coverage anywhere in the diff, and no tests are added for the rewritten Execute/TablesList stub wiring. A future change that fixes enableSqlExpressions' return value (the obvious next commit) can flip the gate with no test catching the inverted-logic or always-false mistakes that already exist in this diff; regressions in the SQL expression path ship unverified.

[ADVISORY] The gate check runs before parsing, returning a generic fmt.Errorf instead of the errutil patterns used elsewhere in ReadQuery, and returns the partially-decoded `eq` alongside the error. Callers of ReadQuery receive both a non-nil result and non-nil error; any caller that checks error first is fine, but the mixed return mirrors an inconsistent error convention (plain fmt.Errorf vs errutil.Base) that produces an unlocalized, non-typed error surfaced to API clients.

[BUG] enableSqlExpressions returns false on every code path, so the featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions flag can never enable SQL expressions Even with FlagSqlExpressions enabled, ReadQuery always returns the error 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' for QueryTypeSQL; the `enabled` variable and the `if enabled { return false }` branch are dead logic — the flag check exists but is wired to a constant outcome, making the gate untestable and the flag inert

[BUG] The new stub DB returns 'not implemented' from every method, silently degrading every previously working SQL expression execution path Any caller of TablesList, RunCommands, or QueryFramesInto that previously executed real DuckDB queries via go-duck now unconditionally fails at runtime; the diff replaces a working implementation with a guaranteed-failing stub while leaving the call sites (sql_command.go Execute, parser.go TablesList) live in the codebase

[BUG] TablesList now calls the stub NewInMemoryDB whose RunCommands always errors, breaking the existing TablesList API with no feature gate or guard Unlike the SQL query path in reader.go (which is flag-gated), TablesList has no feature check, so all existing callers of pkg/expr/sql.TablesList get a hard 'not implemented' error immediately on deploy — an unconditional regression hidden inside a 'framework' PR

[BUG] SQLCommand.Execute now invokes the stub DB's QueryFramesInto, which always returns 'not implemented', so any SQLCommand that reaches Execute fails unconditionally Previously existing SQL expression commands that executed real queries now always log 'Failed to query frames' and return an error result to users; the only gate is in reader.go, and that gate itself always blocks (see reader.go finding), so the entire QueryTypeSQL feature is dead — including for users it worked for before this diff

[ADVISORY] The diff removes the go-duck dependency and its transitive deps while shipping only unimplemented stubs, so the PR deletes a working capability it does not replace The stated intent ('Advanced SQL Analytics Framework') does not trace to any working functionality in this diff: the parser stub, DB stub, and always-false flag gate together mean the only observable behavior change is breaking the existing SQL expression feature; this under-scoped change should either ship the flag-gated replacement or be split so the dependency removal lands with a working implementation

[ADVISORY] The error message 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' is returned to the request path as a runtime error rather than treating the feature as disabled Users issuing SQL-type expressions get a server-side 'not implemented' error string (potentially surfaced as a 500-style internal error rather than a clean validation/feature-disabled response); callers cannot distinguish 'flag off' from 'feature missing', complicating rollout and support diagnostics

[BUG] enableSqlExpressions is written so it can only ever return false: it computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)` (an inverted check), then `if enabled { return false }` followed by an unconditional `return false`, so both the flag-enabled and flag-disabled paths return false. Every SQL expression query is rejected with the error "sqlExpressions is not implemented" regardless of whether FlagSqlExpressions is enabled — the feature gate is dead code and the feature can never be turned on via the flag it was built for.

[BUG] Replacing duck.NewInMemoryDB() with the stub sql.NewInMemoryDB() makes every SQLCommand execution fail: QueryFramesInto unconditionally returns errors.New("not implemented") (pkg/expr/sql/db.go:17-19), whereas the previous go-duck implementation actually executed the query. All existing server-side SQL expression queries that previously returned frames now return an error to every caller on upgrade — a silent functional regression shipped because the dependency was removed without an equivalent implementation, and there is no feature-flag guard on this path to disable it.

[BUG] TablesList now calls the stub NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands, which returns errors.New("not implemented") (pkg/expr/sql/db.go:10-12), instead of the previous working duckDB implementation. Any caller of pkg/expr/sql.TablesList (e.g. to validate/extract table references from SQL expressions) now always gets an error, breaking that dependency-free path the same way sql_command.go is broken.

[ADVISORY] The feature-flag gate lives only in the reader (ReadQuery/QueryTypeSQL branch) while the actual execution path (SQLCommand.Execute in pkg/expr/sql_command.go) constructs and calls the stub DB with no gating, splitting the flag decision and the guarded behavior across two unrelated sites. The next caller of SQLCommand.Execute (or a second construction site) bypasses the flag check entirely, so the flag no longer controls whether the (currently broken, later real) SQL execution path is reachable; the boundary between 'gate' and 'capability' is not owned by one place.

[ADVISORY] The entire new pkg/expr/sql.DB is a ships-inert stub: TablesList, RunCommands, and QueryFramesInto all return 'not implemented', and no code path in the diff can ever produce a successful result from it. The removal of go-duck leaves a placeholder that cannot satisfy either of its two call sites (parser.go TablesList, sql_command.go Execute); merging this ships a broken capability under a feature flag whose own check is also broken, rather than deferring the removal until the replacement DB exists.

[ADVISORY] The local variable is named `enabled` but holds the negation of the flag check (`enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)`), making the name mean its opposite. The next editor reading `if enabled { return false }` will most plausibly 'fix' the apparent contradiction by removing the negation or the early return, changing the flag semantics silently — the confusable binding between the variable name and its value is the trap here.

[ADVISORY] Removing github.com/scottlepp/go-duck also drops transitive deps (apache/thrift, JohnCGriffin/overflow, klauspost/asmfmt, minio/asm2plan9s, minio/c2goasm) whose h1 lines are moved to go.work.sum rather than deleted, leaving the workspace checksum state carrying entries for modules no longer required by the main module. Whoever next runs `go mod tidy` against the workspace sees churn in go.work.sum / go.sum; the module graph no longer matches what the sum files record, making future dependency edits noisier and review of dependency changes harder.

[BUG] enableSqlExpressions returns false unconditionally (and its feature check is inverted: enabled := !IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)), so SQL expressions are rejected even when the sqlExpressions feature flag is enabled. The gate silently drifts from 'feature-flagged' to 'permanently disabled': operators who enable FlagSqlExpressions still get "sqlExpressions is not implemented" on every SQL expression query, and no code path can ever execute the feature — the objective was changed by iteration without explicit human acceptance.

[BUG] SQLCommand.Execute now calls the new stub sql.NewInMemoryDB whose QueryFramesInto unconditionally returns errors.New("not implemented"), replacing the previously functional go-duck DuckDB engine. Every SQL expression command executed by the expression pipeline fails at runtime with 'not implemented' — an accepted, working capability (previously backed by github.com/scottlepp/go-duck, which this diff removes from go.mod) is silently degraded to a guaranteed error for all users, not just when the flag is off.

[BUG] TablesList now runs its json_serialize_sql command against the stub DB, whose RunCommands always returns errors.New("not implemented"), so TablesList can no longer succeed for any input. Any caller of pkg/expr/sql.TablesList gets a hard error on every invocation; the diff removes the only implementation (duck.NewInMemoryDB) and swaps in a stub, silently breaking this exported entry point without an accepted deprecation decision.

[ADVISORY] The new sql.DB ships as a fully inert feature: every method returns 'not implemented' and no writer anywhere in the diff provides a real implementation, while the go-duck dependency it replaced is deleted. Review iterations left the tree with a placeholder masquerading as the 'Advanced SQL Analytics Framework' deliverable — future implementers must rediscover the intended contract from call sites, and the removal of go-duck is irreversible without a new engine; anyone merging this believes SQL analytics shipped when only a rejection gate did.

[ADVISORY] The guard returns the pre-read empty eq alongside a generic "sqlExpressions is not implemented" error, and the check result is computed via an inverted boolean that the function then ignores (dead branch 'if enabled { return false }' before the unconditional 'return false'). The next change to this gate (wiring the flag in properly) must untangle both the inverted condition and the unreachable branch; as written the code reads as if flag state matters when it does not, increasing the risk the flag is later wired inverted again and silently flips behavior for existing users.

[BUG] enableSqlExpressions computes the flag check inverted (!IsEnabledGlobally) and then unconditionally returns false, so the function always returns false regardless of the feature flag's value. SQL expressions are permanently disabled for every tenant even when an admin enables featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions; the flag is a dead control — the gate the diff appears to add provides no runtime off-switch/on-switch, and if the unconditional return is later 'fixed' to return true the inverted ! will silently flip the flag's meaning, enabling the feature when the flag is OFF (a control compared in the wrong polarity).

[ADVISORY] TablesList builds a DuckDB command by string interpolation (fmt.Sprintf("SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')", rawSQL)) with only single-quote doubling as escaping, and the same pattern remains the intended shape of this code path. Any future caller that wires TablesList/RunCommands to a real engine (today the stub in pkg/expr/sql/db.go returns 'not implemented', so the sink is inert) inherits a quote-doubling-only sanitizer; rawSQL comes from user-supplied SQL expressions, and quote-doubling does not neutralize all DuckDB string/dollar-quoting variants, so re-enabling the real DB resurrects a SQL/command injection sink with no parameterization — the next change gets riskier because the unsafe construction is now canonical in-tree.

[ADVISORY] SQLCommand.Execute now routes every SQL expression query to the stub NewInMemoryDB whose QueryFramesInto unconditionally returns errors.New("not implemented"), while the reader gate (reader.go) independently blocks the same path. Two parallel, hand-maintained kill switches for the same feature: when someone later flips the reader gate to honor the flag, they must separately remember to replace the stub in db.go, or every SQL expression query fails at runtime with 'not implemented' surfaced to users via rsp.Error; conversely the double gating means the flag's deny posture is enforced in one place only by accident, and the parser.go TablesList path (which does not go through the reader gate) is reachable with a real DB without any flag check at all.

[BUG] enableSqlExpressions() unconditionally returns false regardless of the feature flag, because its only two return paths are both `return false`. Every SQL expression query is rejected with the error "sqlExpressions is not implemented" even when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled, so the feature gate in ReadQuery (lines 129-133) is dead scaffolding; any test written against this code would have to assert the failure path, not the intended enabled behavior.

[BUG] The error message "sqlExpressions is not implemented" is returned when the feature flag IS enabled (the `enabled == true` guard passes), so the message asserts the opposite of the actual condition. Operators who enable FlagSqlExpressions get a confusing 'not implemented' error, and any test asserting on this error string would encode the wrong semantic (that the flag is disabled) into the suite.

[BUG] The replacement DB stub returns errors.New("not implemented") from TablesList, RunCommands, and QueryFramesInto, so every SQL expression path now fails unconditionally. pkg/expr/sql/parser.go TablesList (line 22-31) always errors after building the json_serialize_sql command, and SQLCommand.Execute (pkg/expr/sql_command.go line 103) always sets rsp.Error, making the previously-working duck-backed SQL expression feature permanently broken with no test in the diff asserting either the break or any replacement behavior.

[BUG] Execute now calls the stub NewInMemoryDB whose QueryFramesInto always errors, so the diff changes the function from executing real SQL to always returning an error result with zero corresponding test changes. Any user query using the SQL expression data source always receives an error result; the change is behavior-bearing (real DB swapped for a always-failing stub) yet no test file in the diff exercises this transition, so existing tests that passed against go-duck would now fail — or worse, tests asserting rsp.Error exist silently and validate the broken path.

[ADVISORY] The double-negation `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)` combined with the unconditional `return false` makes the function a tautology that no assertion could meaningfully distinguish from a constant false. A test for this function can only ever assert 'returns false', giving false confidence that the feature flag is wired correctly when it is not; the next change risks silently inverting the gate.

[BUG] enableSqlExpressions() unconditionally returns false (both the early return and the final return are `return false`), so the gate in ReadQuery rejects every SQL expression query even when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled. Any dashboard/alert using QueryTypeSQL gets a hard 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' error at read time; the feature flag toggle has no effect, so the shipped flag is inert and the SQL-expression path is dead in production.

[BUG] SQLCommand.Execute now calls sql.NewInMemoryDB().QueryFramesInto, which always returns errors.New("not implemented"), so every previously-working SQL command execution fails at runtime. Existing saved SQL expression queries that worked via go-duck now fail on every execution after this change lands; the drop of github.com/scottlepp/go-duck removes the only working implementation with no replacement wired in.

[BUG] TablesList() now runs against the stub DB and always returns the 'not implemented' error, so the SQL parser's table-extraction path fails unconditionally. Any caller relying on TablesList for parsing/validation gets an error on every invocation; combined with the Execute regression, the entire pkg/expr/sql package is non-functional while its public API still advertises these operations.

[ADVISORY] The ReadQuery gate runs unconditionally for all QueryTypeSQL requests, including on the read path of existing saved queries, instead of being introduced behind an expand/contract rollout that keeps old behavior until the new engine is ready. Rolling deploys and rollbacks behave asymmetrically: a downgrade after this ships leaves previously-stored SQL-expression queries permanently failing until data is rewritten; the check should be gated so old persisted queries still resolve during transition.

[BUG] enableSqlExpressions is written so that it returns false on every path — when the flag is disabled it returns false immediately, and when the flag is enabled the computed `enabled` is false (`enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)` inverts the flag) so it also returns false. Even for deployments that explicitly enable featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions, ReadQuery hits the `if !enabled` branch at line ~129 and returns the error "sqlExpressions is not implemented" for every SQL expression query; the feature flag cannot ever turn the feature on, so all SQL-expression requests fail with the same error as before the flag existed.

[ADVISORY] The new in-process DB stub returns errors.New("not implemented") from TablesList, RunCommands, and QueryFramesInto with no implementation behind them, so pkg/expr/sql/parser.go TablesList and SQLCommand.Execute now always fail at runtime. Every SQL expression or SQL command execution path silently degrades to a guaranteed error with zero signal that this is a deliberate stub versus a regression; if this scaffolding ships before the backing implementation (e.g. a duckdb binding), users get opaque 'not implemented' failures where go-duck previously executed real queries — the removal of github.com/scottlepp/go-duck drops working functionality that is only gated (incorrectly, see reader.go finding) by a flag.

[ADVISORY] The gate returns the error "sqlExpressions is not implemented" when the feature is disabled, which misdescribes the failure: the query was rejected by a feature flag, not by a missing implementation. Operators who see this error in dashboards/logs will conclude the feature needs code work rather than that they need to set the feature flag (or, with the always-false bug, that the flag path is broken), misdirecting debugging of exactly the case this diff introduces.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TablesList builds a DuckDB command by string interpolation (fmt.Sprintf("SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')", rawSQL)) with only single-quote doubling as escaping, and the same pattern remains the intended shape of this code path. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The ReadQuery gate runs unconditionally for all QueryTypeSQL requests, including on the read path of existing saved queries, instead of being introduced behind an expand/contract rollout that keeps old behavior until the new engine is ready. Rolling deploys and rollbacks behave asymmetrically: a downgrade after this ships leaves previously-stored SQL-expression queries permanently failing until data is rewritten; the check should be gated so old persisted queries still resolve during transition.

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/expr/reader.go`, the `QueryTypeSQL` case now always calls `enableSqlExpressions(h)` and returns an error when it is false. The new helper `enableSqlExpressions` is implemented to always return `false` (it returns `false` in both branches), so **all** SQL queries will fail at read time (`return eq, fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")`). This is a concrete broken-behavior regression introduced by the diff, consistent with the finding’s concern that persisted SQL queries would stop resolving during rollout/rollback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] enableSqlExpressions is written so that it returns false on every path — when the flag is disabled it returns false immediately, and when the flag is enabled the computed `enabled` is false (`enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)` inverts the flag) so it also returns false. Even for deployments that explicitly enable featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions, ReadQuery hits the `if !enabled` branch at line ~129 and returns the error "sqlExpressions is not implemented" for every SQL expression query; the feature flag cannot ever turn the feature on, so all SQL-expression requests fail with the same error as before the flag existed.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go, enableSqlExpressions() sets `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns `false` in both the `if enabled` branch and the final return, so it always returns false regardless of the flag state. ReadQuery’s QueryTypeSQL case checks `if !enabled { return eq, fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented") }`, meaning SQL expression queries will always fail with that error and the feature flag can never enable the functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new in-process DB stub returns errors.New("not implemented") from TablesList, RunCommands, and QueryFramesInto with no implementation behind them, so pkg/expr/sql/parser.go TablesList and SQLCommand.Execute now always fail at runtime. Every SQL expression or SQL command execution path silently degrades to a guaranteed error with zero signal that this is a deliberate stub versus a regression; if this scaffolding ships before the backing implementation (e.g. a duckdb binding), users get opaque 'not implemented' failures where go-duck previously executed real queries — the removal of github.com/scottlepp/go-duck drops working functionality that is only gated (incorrectly, see reader.go finding) by a flag.

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces the prior duckdb-backed implementation (github.com/scottlepp/go-duck/duck) with a new pkg/expr/sql/DB stub whose methods TablesList, RunCommands, and QueryFramesInto all unconditionally return `errors.New("not implemented")` (pkg/expr/sql/db.go). As a result, `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go` now calls `NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands(...)` and will fail at runtime, and `SQLCommand.Execute` now calls `sql.NewInMemoryDB().QueryFramesInto(...)` and will also always fail. Additionally, `enableSqlExpressions` in pkg/expr/reader.go returns false on all paths, so QueryTypeSQL reads now always error with `sqlExpressions is not implemented`, further ensuring SQL expressions cannot work. This is a concrete behavior regression shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The gate returns the error "sqlExpressions is not implemented" when the feature is disabled, which misdescribes the failure: the query was rejected by a feature flag, not by a missing implementation. Operators who see this error in dashboards/logs will conclude the feature needs code work rather than that they need to set the feature flag (or, with the always-false bug, that the flag path is broken), misdirecting debugging of exactly the case this diff introduces.

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/expr/reader.go`, the new SQL gate returns `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")` when `enableSqlExpressions(h)` is false. That message attributes the failure to missing implementation rather than feature-flag rejection, which is misleading for operators/debugging. This is grounded in the diff regardless of the separate (also real) issue that `enableSqlExpressions` currently always returns false.
